findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:1869-1873 — the deadline reconciler maps providerLaunchState==='revoked' to REAPED_WITHOUT_SIGNAL (reaped:true, residualProcessGroup:false), yielding replacementSafe=true WITHOUT ever consulting providerIdentity. When a worker wedges before spawning a provider, the launch fence marks the run 'revoked' while a live worker is still mid-flight; revocation only proves the framework never GRANTED launch authority and cannot distinguish 'never launched' from 'revoked while a live worker could still spawn'. The run then reports a clean reap that never happened. Reproduced deterministically 5/5 with an isolated probe: state=timed_out, providerIdentity=null, replacementSafe=true, processCleanup={reaped:true,residualProcessGroup:false}. This directly violates CHK-001:adversarial:1 ('replacementSafe false where cleanup cannot be proven') and CHK-003:adversarial:0. Blast radius is real, not cosmetic: replacementSafe gates provider admission-slot release (core/host-run.ts:1690) and is a REQUIRED precondition for managed review evidence import (core/managed-review-evidence.ts:313) and cross-host verdict acceptance (handlers/cross-host-review.ts:407), so a false 'safe' can release a slot and admit evidence while an unidentified provider may still be able to write results.

All 58 verificationEvidence records are mechanical receipts (exit code 0 + outputDigest + selectorMatched) captured at executedAt 2026-08-16T14:47:12Z, but the attested suites FAIL on re-execution against the identical materialHash 85ebcbe2bf30. Observed failures: 'missing provider identity remains honestly unsafe after deadline convergence' (managed-host-run-smoke.ts:647) and 'PID/PGID fingerprint ambiguity must never authorize replacement' (managed-host-run-smoke.ts:297, managed-host-run-process-smoke.ts:323). The receipts are therefore not reproducible evidence for the intents they are bound to. The evidence bookkeeping shows 0 gaps, so this defect is invisible at the coverage layer and only appears on re-execution — meaning the coverage gate can pass while the attested behavior is broken.

The replacementSafe safety suites are non-deterministic, so they intermittently HIDE the defect above rather than reliably detecting it. Serial re-runs: managed-host-run-smoke failed 1/5 in one batch and 2/3 in another; managed-host-run-process-smoke failed 1/5; provider-process-registry-smoke failed 2/5, surfacing BOTH assertions across different suites because the aggregates share child smokes. The same two assertions migrate between suites depending on timing. Because CHK-007:adversarial:0's aggregate (managed-cross-provider-suite-smoke) treats any child exit 0 as PASS, a lucky scheduling run produces a green mechanical receipt for a broken safety property. These races must be made deterministic or the receipts they produce cannot be trusted as gate evidence.

All 58 evidence notes are formulaic template strings ('Tool-executed <X> receipt covers <intentRef> against the current Story material') that never name the behavior verified, and all 58 intents resolve to only 10 whole-suite selectors that are terminal PASS banners (e.g. 'managed-host-run-smoke PASS' covers 8 distinct intents; 'managed-review-evidence-smoke PASS' covers 11). A suite-terminal banner cannot discriminate WHICH intent passed, so the receipt cannot distinguish a suite that asserts an intent from one that silently omits it. This is the review-rule-3 'broad description' pattern. I verified by source inspection that the specific sub-claims (silent-but-live, worker crash, TERM-resistant escalation to KILL, ledger-off contention, candidate overflow, EPIPE) do have real assertions, so this is a traceability weakness rather than a fabricated-coverage finding — but it is precisely what allowed the two failing safety assertions above to sit behind green receipts.

Full reads were bounded to the story coverage artifacts plus the one anomalous 52-line aggregate suite; the remaining large smoke suites (host-run-usage-smoke 3496 lines, managed-review-evidence-smoke 2520, cross-host-review-smoke 2080, managed-host-run-smoke 1273) and production modules were triaged by targeted grep plus direct re-execution and an isolated runtime probe rather than full reads, since executable behavior — not source prose — is the authoritative coverage evidence for this lane.
